title: Choosing Data Structures for Problems
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.answer: Two different keys map to the same bucket.
options: Two different keys map to the different bucket.
Two same keys map to the same bucket.
Two different keys map to the same bucket.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Two different keys map to the same bucket.

questions.prompt: When can linked-list insertion be O(1)?
questions.answer: When a reference to the insertion node is already known.
options: There is not enough information to determine the result.
When a reference to the insertion node is already known.
When a reference to the insertion node is not already known.
questions.feedback: Model answer: When a reference to the insertion node is already known.

questions.prompt: What is a BST's advantage when balanced?
questions.answer: Ordered search can require O(log n) comparisons.
options: Ordered search can require O(log n) comparisons.
Ordered search cannot require O(log n) comparisons.
There is not enough information to determine the result.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Ordered search can require O(log n) comparisons.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: operation — Action such as lookup or insertion.
random access — Direct access by numeric index.
trade-off — A benefit weighed against a cost.

blocks.title: Discover
blocks.text: Choose structures from operations first, not familiar names: indexed access, insertion, deletion, queue discipline or key lookup.

blocks.title: Trace
blocks.text: Consider runtime and additional memory: arrays/lists support indexed access; linked lists can insert cheaply given a node; dictionaries use extra bucket storage.

blocks.title: Evaluate
blocks.text: Justify the suitability for a real task, including constraints and the cost of maintaining the structure.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain the trace
blocks.text: Stack (LIFO): the most recently visited earlier page is retrieved first. Browser navigation may use multiple stacks for back/forward.
